messages:
Maya: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a synthetic traffic generator (SpikeChorus) for kernel selection + batching heuristic A/Bs. Goal: apples-to-apples perf comparisons across fp16 / int8 / q4 variants while exercising KV cache and warmup behavior.
Simon: Nice. High level — how are you modeling KV warmup? that usually skews tail numbers.
Maya: Plan is 3 modes: cold-start, steady-state, and replay-with-prefix. Cold = no KV warmup. Steady = continuous synthetic clients with a configurable "kv_warmup_pct" ramp. Replay-with-prefix = feed recorded traces but prepend synthetic prefixes to reach desired KV fill.
Ekaterina: For apples-to-apples we should fix: token distribution, seq length distro, and request inter-arrival distribution. Otherwise kernel-selection differences get confounded with workload shape.
Maya: Agreed. Implementation is config-driven. Example generator config (YAML):
```
seed: 42
clients: 500
qps_profile:
  ramp_seconds: 120
  start_qps: 10
  peak_qps: 2000
burst_shape: gated_sawtooth
burst_params:
  duty_cycle: 0.12
  pulse_ms: 75
seq_length_distribution: 
  type: histogram
  buckets: [8, 16, 32, 64, 128]
kv_warmup_pct: 0.6
batch_window_ms: 8
kernel_targets: ["fp16", "q4_0", "int8"]
replay_mode: false
```
Simon: Sweet. Two quick asks: 1) expose per-client sticky seeds so we can reproduce a client-shaped KV collision; 2) ability to pin batch-window to emulate very aggressive batching (1-2ms) vs conservative (20ms).
Maya: Both doable. Sticky seed will be --client-seed offset. batch_window_ms already plumbed in.
Ryan: For measurement, capture: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, jit-compile time (first N requests), kernel switch overhead, and batching distribution (histogram of batch sizes). Also collect NVTX traces for hot path.
Maya: Yes — we add counters emitted to /metrics: synth.batch_sizes, synth.kv_hits, synth.kernel_switches, synth.kernel_switch_latency_ms.
Perf-Bot: smoke-run finished: config=spike-chorus-default, kernel=q4_0, batch_window_ms=8 -> p95 increased 12% vs fp16 baseline, p99 +18%. logs: s3://redwood-perf/spike-chorus/2398765432/log.tgz
Simon: Oof. Can you rerun with kv_warmup_pct=1.0 (fully warmed) to see how much of tail is KV-induced?
Perf-Bot: queued rerun (kv_warmup_pct=1.0). ETA ~ 4m.
Maya: If rerun shows improvement then we know it's cache behavior; else look at kernel micro-ops (quantized kernel may have worse small-batch path).
Ekaterina: Suggest an experiment matrix: rows = kernel_targets, cols = batch_window_ms values, each cell run with 3 kv_warmup_pct values (0.0, 0.6, 1.0) and both ramp vs burst traffic. That should highlight where heuristics fail.
Maya: I'll generate a job matrix and a harness script. sample run command (dev):
```bash
./run_synth --config configs/spike-chorus.yaml --kernel q4_0 --batch-window 8 --kv-warmup 0.6 --out /tmp/run2398765432
```
Simon: Can we also add an optional "reorder_requests" flag to stress QoS and batching heuristics? sometimes request arrival jitter changes batch formation.
Maya: yeah we'll add reorder seed and jitter_ms.
Ryan: After runs, produce an apples-to-apples CSV with these columns: kernel, batch_window_ms, kv_warmup_pct, p50, p90, p95, p99, mean_batch_size, compile_overhead_ms, notes. Then post to /perf/dashboard for visualization.
Maya: Will do. I'll kick off the matrix tomorrow morning and tag results here. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
